subject.summary: An updated block pool home: remodeled kitchen with quartz counters, updated baths, new flooring, and a new roof the listing dates to this year, put on while the home was off the market.

summary_page.label: Buyer Summary
summary_page.headline: Open at the bottom of what recent sales support: after months on the market and repeated price cuts, you have room to negotiate.
why: The closest Cattail Crossing pool sales, adjusted to this home, center near the middle of the range.
The market cooled since early in the year: homes now sell under their original asking price, and most sellers pay part of buyers' costs.
Months on the market and repeated price cuts give you room to negotiate price or a seller credit.

AC, water heater and pool equipment ages
Kitchen, baths and any plumbing work
summary_page.next_step: Get the listing agent's answers on the roof permit and the system ages, then write the offer.

bottom_line.why: The two sales that support this price closed earlier in the year, when mortgage rates were lower and homes were selling faster. The recent sales and this home's own price cuts point toward the middle of the range.

events.note: Taken off the market; new roof installed, per the listing

history.takeaway: The market has had a long look at this home at a higher price, and no buyer has gone under contract. The new roof answers one question buyers had, but we need its permit and final inspection before writing an offer.

offer_plan.why_opening: The bottom of the supported range, backed by the comps. After this long on the market and this many price cuts, the seller has reason to counter rather than ignore it.
offer_plan.why_target: Where the recent sales and the typical negotiation off asking suggest this home settles.
offer_plan.why_walk_away: Just under the median of the adjusted comps. Above it you'd be paying earlier prices and risking a low appraisal you'd have to cover in cash.
offer_plan.conditions: the new roof is permitted and passed its final inspection, the inspection finds nothing major in the original systems, and no other offers are competing. If any of those changes, we'll revisit the numbers before you sign.

offer.heading: Negotiating Points
bullets: There is room to negotiate. The price has come down four times for months, and no buyer has gone under contract at any of those prices. Mortgage rates are also higher now than when the earlier sales happened.

Seller help with closing costs is normal right now. Most nearby sales in recent months included seller-paid costs. Asking for a credit instead of a lower price can reduce the cash you need at closing.

Watch the appraisal. Only a couple of similar pool homes nearby have sold above this asking price, both earlier in the year. An offer near the top of the range raises the chance the appraisal comes in low, which you would have to cover in cash or renegotiate.

comps.intro: We looked at every sale within a mile and chose the closest matches: Cattail Crossing pool homes of about this size, built in the same era. We included the ones that argue against a lower price, and adjusted each sale to what it would have brought as this home.
comps.method_note: Seller-paid costs come off the sale price, since they reduce what the seller actually received. Condition adjustments are based on listing descriptions, not visits, so they are judgment calls.

bullets: Homes are selling under their original asking price, after seller-paid costs, compared with about full price earlier in the year. Sellers now expect to negotiate.
Inventory is balanced. That's neither a buyer's market nor a seller's market, but it has shifted toward buyers, and most current listings have already cut their price.
Mortgage rates are up from the earlier sales. That's the main reason the earlier prices are harder to repeat now.

Price per square foot. This home asks more per square foot than most Cattail Crossing sales. That's supportable for an updated pool home with a new roof, but only a couple of similar sales have been higher.

insurance.drivers: The main things that drive the cost for this house are the new roof (insurers will want its permit date), the AC and water heater if they're original, wind-mitigation features and the pool. Get a flood quote with the homeowners quote, and a real quote during your inspection period, after the four-point and wind-mitigation inspections.

credit_scenarios.takeaway: A credit is worth it if cash is tight or you might sell within a decade, and less so if you have savings to spare and plan to stay long term.

items: The new roof. The listing says the roof was replaced this year, while the home was off the market. Roof age is the biggest factor in insuring a Florida home, so we want the permit, the final inspection and any warranty in writing.
Why the price keeps coming down. Four cuts in four months can simply mean an ambitious first price, but ask whether any buyer's inspection or feedback raised a problem.
Original systems. Neither the AC's nor the water heater's age is listed. If they're original, they're near the end of their life, and insurers ask about both.
Permits for the remodel. Confirm the kitchen, bath, and any plumbing or electrical work was permitted. Unpermitted work can cause problems with insurance and future resale.
The third bath. Check that the property appraiser's record shows three full baths, and if one was added, confirm it was permitted.
Pool equipment and screen enclosure. Neither age is listed. Also confirm the pool has a compliant safety barrier.

"As-Is" doesn't mean no inspection. If the offer is written on the As-Is contract, you still get an inspection period in which you can cancel for any reason. It only means the seller isn't committing to repairs.
questions: Can you share the roof permit, the final inspection, and any roofer's warranty? Is there a new wind-mitigation report?

Is the third full bath original to the house?
Is the seller open to contributing toward the buyer's closing costs?
